• The USSR (now Russia) Constitution served as a model for the Preamble's fundamental duties and the Ideals of justice (social, economic, and political).
 
• Federation with a strong Center, the vesting of residuary powers in the Center, the appointment of state governors by the Center, and advisory jurisdiction of the Supreme Court are characteristics of the Indian Constitution that are modelled after those of the Constitution of Canada.

questions.question: Anant's mother advised him to not sleep under the trees at night as trees release ______ at night.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**release of carbon dioxide.**__

__
 
• The **carbon dioxide** that is produced during **human respiration** reaches the empty spaces within the leaves and simultaneously photosynthesis is going on.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

 
• Due to this, **carbon dioxide **present in the air is used and **consumed by the plants**.
 
• Thus during the day, plants produce oxygen while **consuming carbon dioxide but at the night the process of photosynthesis stops but respiration continues for plants.**
 
 
• Meaning that **oxygen is not produced by the plants at night.**
 
 
 
• Because of this **natural phenomenon, **it is advised that at night if you sleep under the tree, you will not get oxygen, which can cause **breathing problems, suffocation, etc.**

questions.question: Which among the following issues are abolished by the Article 17 of the Indian constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Untouchability**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Article 17- Abolition of Untouchability: 

 
 
• Untouchability is abolished and its practice in any form is forbidden.
 
• In fact, the enforcement of any disability arising out of untouchability shall be an offence punishable in accordance with the law.
 
• Abolition of untouchability has been included among the fundamental rights under article17.
 
• In fact, this is one of the few fundamental rights which is available against individuals.
 
• To make an untouchability law further strong, parliament passed an Untouchability (offences) Act in 1955.
 
• However, this act was further amended and also renamed in the year of 1976 as Protection of the Civil Rights Act, 1955.​
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: By which of the following process does a solid substance is directly converted into gas?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Sublimation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Sublimation: It is the conversion of a solid directly into vapors.
 
 
• Sublimation takes place when the boiling point is less than the melting point.
 
• The heat required to change a unit mass of solid directly into vapors at a given temperature is called the heat of sublimation at that temperature.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Condensation: The process by which water vapor in the air is changed into liquid water is called condensation. This caused the water vapor to condense, or turn into its liquid form.
 
 
• Condensation is crucial to the water cycle because it is responsible for the formation of clouds.
 
 
 
• Evaporation: The vaporization occurring from the free surface of a liquid is called evaporation.
 
 
• Evaporation is the escape of molecules from the surface of a liquid.
 
• This process takes place at all temperatures and increases with the increase of temperature.
 
• Evaporation leads to cooling because the faster molecules escape and, therefore, the average kinetic energy of the molecules of the liquid (and hence the temperature) decreases.
 
 
 
• Diffusion: It is the movement of a substance from an area of high concentration to an area of low concentration. 
 
 
• Diffusion happens in liquids and gases because their particles move randomly from place to place.

questions.question: Sam wants to share his presentation with larger audience via emails. Which feature of MS PowerPoint 365 can he use for it?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is S__**hare**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Collaboration and Accessibility: The "Share" feature in MS PowerPoint 365 allows Sam to collaborate with others and make the presentation accessible to a wider audience. He can easily share the presentation with multiple people, enabling them to view and collaborate on the same document simultaneously.
 
• Email Sharing: Within the "Share" feature, Sam can select the option to share the presentation via email. This allows him to send the presentation directly to the intended recipients' email addresses.
 
• Recipient Permissions: MS PowerPoint 365 provides options for specifying the level of permissions for recipients. Sam can choose whether recipients can simply view the presentation or have editing capabilities, depending on his requirements.
 
• Real-Time Updates: When Sam shares the presentation via email using MS PowerPoint 365, recipients can access and view the latest version of the presentation in real-time. Any changes made by Sam or other collaborators will be reflected immediately for all recipients.
 
• Collaboration Tools: The "Share" feature also includes collaboration tools that enable recipients to add comments, suggest edits, or make revisions directly within the presentation. This facilitates effective collaboration and feedback exchange among the larger audience.
 
• OneDrive Integration: MS PowerPoint 365 integrates with OneDrive, Microsoft's cloud storage service. When Sam shares the presentation via email, he can choose to store the file on OneDrive and provide recipients with a link to access it. This ensures that everyone has access to the most up-to-date version of the presentation.
 
• Security and Privacy: The "Share" feature in MS PowerPoint 365 includes various security measures to protect the presentation and ensure privacy. Sam can control who has access to the presentation, and he can also set passwords or expiration dates for the shared link to enhance security.
 
• Version History: MS PowerPoint 365 keeps a version history of the shared presentation. This means that Sam can easily revert to previous versions if needed or track the changes made by collaborators.
 
• Outlook Integration: If Sam uses Microsoft Outlook as his email client, the "Share" feature seamlessly integrates with it. He can share the presentation directly from within PowerPoint 365, leveraging the familiar email interface of Outlook.

questions.question: Which of the following is not an important river of Malwa plateau?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mahanadi river**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__ **

__
 
• River Mahanadi originates from Sihawa Mountain near a village in Raipur, Chhattisgarh.
 
• The Mahanadi River system is the third largest in peninsular India after Godavari and Krishna, and the largest river in Odisha state.
 
 
• The Mahanadi (“Great River”) follows a total course of 560 miles (900 km) and has an estimated drainage area of 51,000 square miles (132,100 square km).
 
• The catchment area of the river extends to Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh, Odisha, Jharkhand, and Maharashtra.
 
• Tributaries
 
 
• Seonath, Hasdeo, Mand, and Ib join Mahanadi from the left whereas,
 
• Ong, Tel, and Jonk join it from the right.
 
 
 
• At Sambalpur, the Hirakud Dam on the river (the longest dam in India) has formed a man-made lake 35 miles (55 km) long; the dam has several hydroelectric generators. 
 
 
 
• It enters the Odisha plains near Cuttack and enters the Bay of Bengal at False Point by several channels.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Malwa plateau**__

 __
 
• ​__Indian plateau region known as the Malwa Plateau. It is bordered to the north by the Madhya Bharat Plateau and Bundelkhand Upland, to the east and south by the Vindhya Range, and to the west by the Gujarat Plains. The plateau, which is of volcanic origin, spans southeast Rajasthan state and central Madhya Pradesh state. The Sanskrit word malav is where the name Malwa comes from (part of the abode of Laksmi [goddess of wealth]). The Maurya, Gupta, and Paramara empires alternately dominated the plateau; during this time, numerous Buddhist temples and monuments (such as the stupas at Sanchi), known for their architecture and sculpture, were also constructed. In 1390 CE, the Muslims took control of the plateau, which then belonged to the Maratha empire. It was given to the British in 1817.
 
• The Malwa Plateau has an elevation range of 500 to 600 metres (about 1,650 to 2,000 feet). Sandstone hills and solitary mesas, as well as remnants of old lava flows, may be seen scattered throughout the plateau. The Mahi River drains the western portion of the area, the Chambal River the middle, and the Betwa River and the headwaters of the Dhasan and Ken rivers the eastern portion. Additionally, there are the Parbati, Sipra, Gambhir, and Choti Kali Sindh rivers, all of whose valleys are bordered by terraced hills. Savanna-style vegetation is present, with sporadic teak and sal (Shorea robusta) woods.

questions.question: In India, trees of which forest type shed their leaves for about six to eight weeks in dry summer?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tropical Deciduous Forests**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

Tropical Deciduous Forests:

__
 
• These are the most widespread forests out of all the types of forests in India
 
• Also, called Monsoon Forests.
 
• They are found in the regions having rainfall between 70-200cm.
 
• They shed their leaves for about six to eight weeks in dry summer.
 
• Tropical Deciduous Forests are further classified into two types of forests on the basis of rainfall- Tropical Moist Deciduous Forests and Tropical Dry Deciduous Forests.
 
• TROPICAL MOIST DECIDUOUS FORESTS:
 
 
• Present in the areas having rainfall between 100-200cm.
 
• Found in eastern slopes of Western Ghats, foothills of the Himalayas in the North-eastern States and Odisha.
 
• Main Species of Tropical Moist Deciduous Forests: Teak, Sal, Sheshum, amla, Kusum, mahua, Sandalwood, etc.
 
 
 
• TROPICAL DRY DECIDUOUS FORESTS.
 
 
• Found in the areas having rainfall between 70-100cm.
 
• Present in rainier areas of the peninsula and the plains of Uttar Pradesh and Bihar.
 
• During Dry seasons, Trees shed their leaves completely and the forest appears like a Grassland.
 
• Main species of Tropical Dry Deciduous Forests: Khair, Tendu, Palas, axlewood, bel, etc.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__Tropical Evergreen Forests:__

 
• These forests are restricted to heavy rainfall areas of the *Western Ghats and the island groups of Lakshadweep, Andaman, and Nicobar, upper parts of Assam, and Tamil Nadu coast.*
 
• They are at their best in areas having more than 200 cm of rainfall with a short dry season.
 
• The trees reach great heights up to 60 meters or even above.
 
• Since the region is warm and wet throughout the year, it has luxuriant vegetation of all kinds.
 
• The trees, shrubs, and creepers give it a multilayered structure.
 
• There is no definite time for trees to shed their leaves.
 
• As such, these forests appear green all the year-round

 
 

 Vegetation
 Location
 
 

 
 
Tropical Evergreen Forests

 
 The Western Ghats, the island groups of Lakshadweep, Andaman, and Nicobar island.
 
 

 
 
Tropical Deciduous Forests

 
 The northeastern states, along the foothills of the Himalayas, Jharkhand, West Odisha, and Chhattisgarh, and on the eastern slopes of the Western Ghats.

questions.question: Sanchi stupa is located in which states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Madhya Pradesh__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ​Sanchi Stupa:

 
 
• Sanchi is about 50 km from Bhopal, the capital of Madhya Pradesh.
 
• Stupa at Sanchi is a world heritage site. 
 
• It was built by Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE.
 
• It is the most prominent and the oldest and is believed to have the Buddha’s relics.
 
• Along with other relatively small stupas, there are three main stupas at Sanchi.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.britannica.com/36/155836-050-89E7AA9E/Great-Stupa-Sanchi-India.jpg] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• 
 
 
• It is a religious place with historical and archaeological significance.

 
 
• Sanchi is famous in the world for stupas, monolithic Asokan pillar, temples, monasteries and sculptural wealth dating from 3rd century B.C. to 12th century A.D.
 
• During Sunga times, several edifices were raised at Sanchi and its surrounding hills.

questions.question: The National Payments Corporation of India was set up under the provisions of which Act?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) **was set up under the provisions of the **Payment and Settlement Systems Act, of 2007.**
 
• **Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007:**
 
 
• Regulates and supervises payment and settlement systems in India.
 
• **Provides the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) **with the authority to** issue guidelines, set standards, and take action against payment system operators if needed.**
 
• Ensures the safety, security, and efficiency of payment and settlement systems in the country.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The SARFAESI Act, 2002:**

 
 
• Stands for Securitization and Reconstruction of** Financial Assets and Enforcement of Security Interest Act.**
 
• Aims to address non-performing assets (NPAs) in the Indian banking system.
 
• Allows banks and financial institutions to recover loans by auctioning or selling borrowers' assets without intervention from the court.
 
 

 
• **Government Securities Act, 2006:**

 
 
• Governs the issuance, management, and trading of government securities in India.
 
• Streamlines procedures for the issuance of government securities and dematerialization of existing securities.
 
• Aims to protect the interests of investors and promote the development of a stable and efficient market for government securities.
 
 
 
• **Companies Act, 2013:**
 
 
• Governs the formation, regulation, and dissolution of companies in India.
 
• **Replaces the Companies Act, of 1956, **and introduces several new provisions to improve corporate governance and transparency.
 
• Provides guidelines for the functioning of **companies, including rules for incorporation, management, fundraising, auditing, and the responsibilities of directors and other key personnel.**

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is correct regarding the socialist society in the economy?

I. The government decides what goods are to be produced.

II. Distribution of goods under socialism is supposed to be based on what people need.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **In a socialist society or economy:**

 
 
• The government decides what goods are to be produced.
 
• **Central planning and public ownership of the means of production play** a significant role in determining what goods and services are produced and in what quantities.
 
• The distribution of **goods under socialism is supposed to be based on what people need.**
 
• The aim is to ensure that** everyone's basic needs are met, promoting a more equitable distribution of wealth and reducing income inequality.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Aspect
 Socialist Economy
 Capitalist Economy
 
 
 
 

 Ownership of Means of Production
 Owned and controlled by the state or workers' cooperatives
 Owned and controlled by private individuals or corporations
 
 

 Price Mechanism
 Absent or limited use of market pricing mechanisms
 The central role of market pricing mechanisms in determining prices
 
 

 Distribution of Resources
 Decided by the state or a central planning authority
 Decided by the market forces of supply and demand
 
 

 Economic Inequality
 Strives for economic equality and a more even distribution of resources
 Tolerates economic inequality and rewards individual effort and success
 
 

 Role of Government
 Plays a large role in the economy, regulating and managing the means of production
 Limited role in the economy, primarily enforcing laws and contracts
 
 

 Social Services
 Universal access to healthcare, education, and social services
 Access to healthcare, education, and social services is determined by an individual's ability to pay
 
 

 Innovation and Creativity
 Emphasis on collective innovation and public goods
 Emphasis on individual innovation and private property rights
 
 

 Competition
 Limited competition or controlled competition between state-owned enterprises
 Emphasis on free market competition between private businesses
 
 

 Motivation
 Motivated by the collective good and contributing to society
 Motivated by individual gain and profit
 
 

 Efficiency
 May suffer from inefficiencies due to central planning or lack of competition

questions.question:
Natural language processing (NLP) is a branch of artificial intelligence that helps computers ______ human language.

I. understand

II. Interpret

III. manipulate
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**I, II and III**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Natural Language Processing (NLP) **is a **subfield of artificial intelligence and computational linguistics. **
 
• It focuses on the interaction between computers and humans through natural language.
 
• **Understanding**: NLP enables computers to comprehend human language as it is spoken or written.
 
 
• This involves understanding the semantics, syntax, and context of the language.
 
 
 
• **Interpretation: **NLP also involves the interpretation of human language by computers.
 
 
• This refers to the process of parsing the input, determining its meaning, and potentially transforming it into another format or language.
 
 
 
• **Manipulation**: Furthermore, NLP allows for the manipulation of human language.
 
 
• This could involve tasks like text generation, translation, summarization, and more.
 
• The combination of understanding, interpretation, and manipulation allows for a wide range of applications.
 
• These include chatbots, sentiment analysis, machine translation, voice recognition, and many more.
 
 
 
• ***Therefore, all three options (I, II, III) are correct. NLP involves the understanding, interpretation, and manipulation of human language by computers.***
 
• The development and refinement of NLP technologies are continually evolving, making human-computer interactions more natural, intuitive, and effective.
 
• Overall, the goal of NLP is to make computers as proficient as possible at understanding and responding to** human language, allowing for more natural and intuitive human-computer interaction.**

questions.question: Which of the following is not a subgroup of plant kingdom?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hemichordata**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hemichordata is not a subgroup of the plant kingdom.**

 
 
• Hemichordata is a** phylum within the animal kingdom, which includes species like acorn worms and graptolites.**
 
• Hemichordates are a group of marine invertebrates that are distantly related to **echinoderms (such as starfish and sea urchins) and chordates (which include vertebrates like fish, birds, and mammals).**
 
• Hemichordates are divided into two main groups: the acorn worms** (Enteropneusta) and the colonial filter feeders (Pterobranchia).**
 
• Acorn worms are typically solitary and burrow in** sediment, while pterobranchs live in colonies attached to hard substrates.**
 
• **Hemichordates exhibit a range of body plans, from worm-like to more complex, colony-forming structures.**
 
• They have a number of **unique features, including a proboscis that can be used for feeding and respiration, and a structure called the stomochord that is thought to be homologous to the notochord in chordates.**
 
• **Hemichordates **have been studied for their potential as model organisms in evolutionary and developmental biology, as well as for their ecological roles in marine ecosystems.
 
• **Example:**
 
 
• Acorn worms (Enteropneusta)
 
• Pterobranchs (Pterobranchia)
 
• Graptolites (Graptolithina)
 
• Cephalodiscus
 
• Xenoturbella
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Thallophyta:**

 
 
• **​**This group includes algae, which are simple, typically unicellular organisms that photosynthesize as plants do.
 
 
 
• **Angiosperms:**
 
 
• **​**These are flowering plants, which produce seeds that are enclosed within a fruit. They are the most diverse group of land plants.
 
 
 
• **Pteridophyta:**
 
 
• **​**This group includes ferns and their allies. They don't produce seeds or flowers; instead, they reproduce and disperse via spores.
 
 

e2:T

• The day is celebrated in honour of the remarkable contribution of the famous Indian scientist and statistician PC Mahalanobis in the field of economic planning and statistical development.

• The formula is used to find the distance between a point and a distribution, based on measurements in multiple dimensions.

questions.question: Which among the following festivals marks the birthday of a great Buddhist saint Je Tsongkhapa?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Galdan Namchot**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The festival that marks the birthday of the great Tibetan Buddhist saint Je **Tsongkhapa is Galdan Namchot.**
 
• This festival also marks the start of the **New Year celebrations in Ladakh, India.**
 
• **Je Tsongkhapa** was a famous** teacher of Tibetan Buddhism whose activities led to the formation of the Gelug school of Tibetan Buddhism.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sarhul: **

 
 
• Sarhul is a **tribal festival celebrated by the ethnic groups in the Indian states of Jharkhand, Odisha, and Chhattisgarh.**
 
• This festival is celebrated to mark the beginning of the new year and the arrival of spring.
 
• Sarhul is celebrated with** traditional music and dance, the worship of village deities, and the sharing of a local drink made from fermented rice or salap.**
 
 
 
• **Losar:**
 
 
• Losar is the Tibetan word for** "New Year," and it is the most important holiday in Tibet and Tibetan** **border Indian states.**
 
• It is celebrated for** 15 days, with the main celebrations on the first three days.**
 
• Losar involves ceremonies, rituals, prayers, and cultural performances, and it is a time to spend with family and friends, to exchange gifts, and to eat special foods.
 
 
 
• **Tusu:**
 
 
• Tusu is a harvest festival celebrated in the Indian states of** Jharkhand, West Bengal, and Odisha.**
 
• The festival is observed on Makar Sankranti, which usually falls on **January 14th or 15th, marking the end of the winter season and the arrival of longer days.**
 
• Tusu involves singing traditional songs, dancing, and offering prayers to **Tusu, a folk deity, for a good harvest and prosperity in the coming year.**
